items.name: BAND_DYN_MODES
items.doc: The side of the threshold the band acts on. Above acts when the band is loud, taming a resonance that only rings when pushed; below acts when it is quiet, lifting a band that drops out. The order is the integer the kernel reads: above is 0, below is 1.

items.name: BAND_DYN_KNEE_DB

source.origin: omx-dsp test/fx/band_dyn.test.c:23 (KNEE_DB 6.0f) holds the same number and reads it from the header once it is declared

items.doc: The soft knee of the band's gain computer, in dB. One knee for the one band-dynamics word, shared by every stage that runs it, the de-esser included: a second spelling of 6 would be a second place where the reduction starts.

items.name: BAND_DYN_MAX_BANDS

source.origin: the operator band reserve, read from OPERATOR_EQ_BANDS_RESERVE

items.doc: How many dynamic bands a channel may hold. A dynamic band is an operator band, so the capacity is the operator's reserve, read and not typed again.

items.name: DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS

source.origin: the value core declares as DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS

items.doc: The shortest attack, in ms, at which the compressor's detector does not alias. Below it the compressor engages its 4x control path, which adds 72 samples of latency; a zero-latency band has no such path, so its attack travel stops at this floor.

items.name: BAND_DYN_THRESHOLD_RANGE

source.origin: the de-esser's threshold travel spread as it is, { ...DEESS_THRESHOLD_RANGE }

items.doc: Where the band starts to act, in dB of the band's own level and not the strip's. It is the same fact the de-esser's threshold is, so it carries the same travel.

items.name: BAND_DYN_RATIO_RANGE

source.origin: the de-esser's ratio travel with the default overridden to 2, { ...DEESS_RATIO_RANGE, default: 2 }

items.doc: How hard the band is held once it is past its threshold. 2:1 rather than the de-esser's 4:1, because a dynamic band is corrective, not a limiter for a sibilant.

items.name: BAND_DYN_RANGE_RANGE

source.origin: the floor read as DEESS_RANGE_RANGE.min, the ceiling +12 (open question 2)

items.doc: The most the band may add to its static gain, signed: below zero the deepest cut, above zero the largest boost. The ceiling of +12 keeps static plus dynamic inside the EQ's own travel. Zero makes the band inert without switching it off.

items.name: BAND_DYN_ATTACK_RANGE

source.origin: min DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS, max COMP_LIMITS.attackMs.max, step as DEESS_ATTACK_RANGE

items.doc: The detector's attack, in ms. The travel stops at the oversampling floor, below which the band would need the compressor's delayed control path.

items.name: BAND_DYN_RELEASE_RANGE

source.origin: min DEESS_RELEASE_RANGE.min, max COMP_LIMITS.releaseMs.max, step DEESS_RELEASE_RANGE.step

items.doc: The detector's release, in ms. 100 ms is long enough not to modulate a 40 Hz band inside four cycles.
